div.p: With the growing demand for real-time communication in industries, Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) has become crucial for ensuring low latency. However, transient transmission failures may still affect reliability and are typically mitigated through redundancy. Existing fault-tolerance studies either rely on a single redundancy approach or fail to adequately address the trade-off between redundancy and network schedulability. This paper investigates a fault-tolerant scheduling problem under the Cyclic Queuing Forwarding (CQF) mechanism and proposes a novel scheduling algorithm. The algorithm integrates both spatial and temporal redundancy to meet the reliability requirements of TSN flows while optimizing schedulability. Specifically, it combines redundancy space exploration with scheduling score calculation to prioritize scheduling decisions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly outperforms existing methods.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: With the continuous development of industrial automation and intelligence, the demand for low-latency and high-reliability communication has surged, which makes strict Quality of Service (QoS) requirements a critical factor [1]. However, traditional Ethernet fails to meet increasingly stringent QoS demands and ensure the stability and reliability of industrial systems. Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) has been introduced to meet the needs of time-sensitive applications by providing deterministic transmission. The IEEE 802.1Qbv standard introduces the Time-Aware Shaper (TAS) mechanism to control traffic on switch ports using predefined Gate Control Lists (GCLs) [2]. However, configuring GCLs requires significant computational resources. To address this problem, the IEEE 802.1Qch standard introduces the Cyclic Queuing and Forwarding (CQF) mechanism [3], which divides time into equal-length time slots and uses a static GCL configuration to reduce computational complexity.

Although CQF guarantees deterministic delay, transient failures during transmission can negatively affect transmission reliability. Existing fault-tolerant approaches for TSN address transient failures through packet replication, which incorporates both spatial and temporal redundancy. Spatial redundancy involves transmitting packet replicas over multiple paths. IEEE 802.1CB introduces Frame Replication and Elimination for Reliability (FRER), which utilizes spatial redundancy [4]. FRER replicates packets at the source and transmits them across disjoint paths, with redundant packets eliminated at the destination. However, excessive use of redundant paths consumes substantial network resources, leading to degraded scheduling performance. To alleviate this, [5] proposes an offline fault-tolerant scheduling algorithm that calculates the upper bound on redundant routes for flows. In [6], the authors present a federated learning-based TSN framework that minimizes failure probability by searching for primary and backup paths. Temporal redundancy, on the other hand, involves transmitting multiple copies of a packet over a single path. The work in [7] introduces a scheduling algorithm that determines the required number of packet copies for each TSN flow. In [8], the authors address fault tolerance under CQF and calculate the upper bound on packet replicas. However, temporal redundancy may result in local resource congestion. The work in [9] proposes a spatiotemporal redundancy scheduling algorithm based on delay bounds. Existing studies, however, either fail to consider redundancy schemes comprehensively or overlook the balance between redundancy and schedulability. This paper addresses the fault-tolerant scheduling problem for TSN flows under CQF and formulates it as an optimization problem with the objective of maximizing network schedulability. A novel heuristic scheduling algorithm is proposed to solve this problem. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm consistently outperforms existing methods.

div.head: III. PROBLEM FORMULATION
div.p: This paper addresses the fault-tolerant scheduling problem under CQF, leveraging both spatial and temporal redundancy to ensure the reliability of TSN flows. Furthermore, injection time offsets play a crucial role in traffic scheduling, and careful selection of these offsets can significantly improve network schedulability. Figure 1 illustrates various scenarios involving redundancy and offsets. The redundancy of 𝑓𝑓 1 is 3, but there are only two available paths in the topology, making it impossible to guarantee reliability with spatial redundancy only. Figure 1 (a) demonstrates a scenario where only temporal redundancy is employed. In this case, the redundancy of 𝑓𝑓 1 exceeds the capacity of a time-slot, causing some packet copies delayed and eventually dropped due to exceeding the delay bound. Figure 1 (b) demonstrates the scenario where both spatial and temporal redundancy are used. Flow 𝑓𝑓 1 uses two paths for transmission, with temporal redundancy adjusted to 𝐿𝐿 1 = {𝐿𝐿 11 = 2, 𝐿𝐿 12 = 1}. Additionally, the injection offset 𝑜𝑜 42 of flow 𝑓𝑓 4 is delayed by one time-slot to ensure the delay requirement of 𝑓𝑓 1 is satisfied. Thus, our primary challenge is to compute the spatial and temporal redundancy and to appropriately select the injection offsets.

div.head: V. EXPERIMENTAL RESULTS
div.p: In this section, we conduct experiments to evaluate the proposed algorithm. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, we compare it with two existing algorithms: FTTS [5] and Ret-FTS [8].

div.head: A. Experiment Settings
div.p: Experiments are conducted on ladder, random, and ring topologies with three network scales: 6, 8, and 10 switches. Each switch is randomly connected to 1 to 3 hosts. The network bandwidth is set to 1000 Mbit/s, the queue capacity is 8 KB, and the time-slot length is 125 µs. The failure parameter 𝜆𝜆 is set to 10 -5 , and the processing and synchronization delay 𝑑𝑑 𝑝𝑝𝑠𝑠 is 20 µs. The proposed algorithm is evaluated using 500 flows, with random source and destination nodes selected from the hosts. Flow periods are set to combinations {2000, 4000} µs, with the delay bound for each flow matching its period. Packet sizes are randomly generated between 64 and 1500 bytes. The PFH value for each flow is randomly selected from 10 -9 , 10 -7 , and 10 -5 . For each parameter set, ten test cases are conducted. The weight parameters 𝛼𝛼 and 𝛽𝛽 are set to -0.5 and 0.5, respectively.

div.head: B. Performance Comparison
div.p: Figure 2 shows the success rate of different algorithms under different queue capacities, which reflects network resource availability. When capacity is limited, Ret-FTS using temporal redundancy causes local congestion, negatively impacting the scheduling success rate. However, when capacity is abundant, FTTS tends to utilize longer paths which increases network resource consumption and results in a lower success rate. In contrast, the proposed algorithm balances both remaining capacity and resource consumption, achieving a higher success rate under different queue resource conditions. Figure 3 illustrates the success rate of different algorithms under different network fault parameters, which directly influence flow redundancy. Larger fault parameters result in more copies. Our algorithm outperforms others in all redundancy scenarios, particularly under high redundancy conditions, as it efficiently allocates time redundancy across paths based on schedule score in high-redundancy scenarios.

div.head: VI. CONCLUSION
div.p: In this paper, we propose an approach that integrates spatial and temporal redundancy to address the fault-tolerant scheduling problem of TSN flows under the CQF mechanism. The approach optimizes flow scheduling by determining scheduling priorities based on redundancy combination scheduling scores. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing methods in terms of scheduling performance and load balancing.
